finding_key: packages/backend/src/datasource/datasource.dto.ts::ssrf: fully user-controlled `host`/`port` are dialed by the server and connection errors are reflected verbatim, allowing internal port/service probing and unix-socket access to the app's own database
evidence: Confirmed in the supplied files: datasource.dto.ts validates `host` only as `@IsString() @Length(1,253)` and `port` as `@IsInt() @Min(1) @Max(65535)` with no allow-list and no rejection of loopback/RFC1918/link-local or a leading `/` (pg treats such a host as a Unix-socket path); createClient() in datasource.service.ts feeds these straight into `new Client(...)`. testConnection() returns `{ success: false, error: (error as Error).message }` and executeQuery() rethrows `pgError.message`, giving exactly the ECONNREFUSED/timeout/SSL-negotiation oracle the claim describes; datasource.controller.ts gates this behind JwtAuthGuard + assertMember, so any authenticated workspace member can drive it. Caveats on weight, not correctness: this is pre-existing code that the diff does not touch (the diff only adds the type parser, SET TimeZone/DateStyle, and tests), and reaching the app's own Postgres additionally requires local trust/peer auth or guessed credentials — though the internal port-probing oracle works regardless.
